Therapy adjustments and close monitoring are recommended in the following scenarios: 1. Rufinamide: This medication reduces the levels or effects of estradiol by influencing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 2. Simvastatin: This drug increases the levels or effects of estradiol by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 3. Sirolimus: Similar to simvastatin, sirolimus increases estradiol levels or effects via the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 4. Somapacitan: Estradiol reduces the effects of somapacitan through mechanisms not fully understood. Oral estrogens may lower the serum IGF-1 response to somapacitan, potentially necessitating higher somapacitan dosages. Refer to the drug monograph for initial dosing recommendations. Therapy adjustments and close monitoring are advised. 5. St. John’s Wort: This herbal supplement decreases estradiol levels or effects by inducing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism and by affecting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid or use alternative therapies due to the significant interaction risk. 6. Stiripentol: This drug affects estradiol metabolism by inhibiting and inducing hepatic enzyme CYP1A2. Stiripentol is a CYP1A2 inhibitor and inducer, requiring close monitoring of co-administered CYP1A2 substrates for potential increased or decreased effects. Dosage adjustments may be necessary. 7. Streptomycin: This antibiotic decreases estradiol levels or effects by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral hormone forms and carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Use caution and monitor closely. 8. Sulfadiazine, Sulfamethoxazole, and Sulfisoxazole: These antibiotics similarly decrease estradiol levels or effects by altering intestinal flora. These interactions apply only to oral hormone forms and carry a low risk of contraceptive failure. Use caution and monitor closely. 9. Tacrolimus: This drug increases estradiol levels or effects via the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 10. Tazemetostat: This medication decreases estradiol levels or effects by inducing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 11. Tecovirimat: This drug decreases estradiol levels or effects by weakly inducing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor sensitive CYP3A4 substrates for effectiveness if co-administered. 12. Teicoplanin and Temocillin: These antibiotics decrease estradiol levels or effects by altering intestinal flora. These interactions apply only to oral hormone forms and carry a low risk of contraceptive failure. Use caution and monitor closely. 13. Teriflunomide: This drug decreases estradiol levels by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP1A2 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 14. Tetracycline and Tigecycline: These antibiotics decrease estradiol levels or effects by altering intestinal flora. These interactions apply only to oral hormone forms and carry a low risk of contraceptive failure. Use caution and monitor closely. 15. Tobramycin: This antibiotic decreases estradiol levels or effects by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral hormone forms and carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Use caution and monitor closely. 16. Tolvaptan: This drug increases estradiol levels or effects via the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 17. Topiramate: This medication decreases estradiol levels or effects by inducing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 18. Trazodone: This drug decreases estradiol levels or effects via the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. The interaction mechanism is unspecified, and its clinical significance is unknown. Monitor closely. 19. Trimethoprim: This antibiotic decreases estradiol levels or effects by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral hormone forms and carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Use caution and monitor closely. 20. Tucatinib: This drug significantly increases estradiol levels or effects by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid concomitant use with CYP3A substrates, as even minimal concentration changes may lead to severe or life-threatening toxicities. If unavoidable, reduce the CYP3A substrate dose per product labeling and monitor closely. 21. Valproic Acid: Estradiol decreases valproic acid levels or effects by increasing its elimination, potentially leading to increased seizure frequency. Therapy adjustments and close monitoring are recommended. 22. Vancomycin: This antibiotic decreases estradiol levels or effects by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral hormone forms and carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Use caution and monitor closely. 23. Verapamil: This drug increases estradiol levels or effects by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism and the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 24. Voriconazole: This antifungal increases estradiol levels or effects by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 25. Warfarin: Estradiol increases the effects of warfarin through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. 26. Zafirlukast: This drug increases estradiol levels or effects by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Additional considerations for estradiol and estrogen therapy include: Gallbladder Disease: Postmenopausal women receiving estrogens may have a 2to 4-fold increased risk of gallbladder disease requiring surgery. Retinal Vascular Thrombosis: Discontinue therapy if sudden vision loss, proptosis, diplopia, or migraines occur. Permanently discontinue if papilledema or retinal vascular lesions are identified. Breast Cancer Risk: Observational studies suggest an increased risk of breast cancer with estrogen plus progestin therapy, and a smaller risk with estrogen-alone therapy, particularly with long-term use. Liver Function: Estrogens may be poorly metabolized in patients with impaired liver function. Discontinue therapy if cholestatic jaundice recurs. Thyroid Hormone Therapy: Patients on thyroid hormone replacement may require increased doses when receiving estrogens. Monitor thyroid function to maintain appropriate free thyroid hormone levels. Hypocalcemia: Estrogen-induced hypocalcemia may occur in women with hypoparathyroidism. Pregnancy and Breastfeeding: Estrogens are not indicated during pregnancy and may reduce milk production in breastfeeding women. Consider the benefits of breastfeeding alongside the mother’s clinical needs and potential risks to the child. This summary provides detailed, professional guidance on estradiol interactions and considerations for safe use.
